title: Contract-version negotiation conformance case
description: One case. Three kinds, because the specification has three separable assertions: the algorithm (negotiate), the frame's parsing (hello), and the manifest-versus-hello agreement (declaration). A runner reads `kind` and dispatches.

local.description: negotiate only. This peer's declared set. Entries are deliberately unconstrained: several cases assert a malformed member is refused rather than skipped.

remote.description: negotiate only. The other peer's declared set, on the same terms.

frame.description: hello only. One decoded frame, without its terminating LF. A string rather than a parsed object, because what is under test is the parsing.

manifest.description: declaration only. The manifest's declared value, or absent to exercise the default. Any JSON value: a case asserts a non-array is refused.

hello.description: declaration only. The set the running peer announced. Well-formed by construction — malformed frames are the hello kind's business.

expect.description: The required outcome. `ok` false requires `exit`, so no refusal case can omit the reserved code.

version.description: negotiate only, on success: the agreed major.

contractVersions.description: hello only, on success: the parsed set, in the order the frame declared it.

reason.description: On refusal. The negotiate kind uses the first two; hello uses those plus the frame reasons; declaration uses declaration-mismatch.

exit.description: The exit code a connector MUST terminate with. Carried as data on every refusal so a binding that owns a process is held to it by the corpus rather than by prose.
